figures.label: fig-runge-phenomenon
figures.caption: The Runge phenomenon: polynomial interpolation of $f(x) = 1/(1 + 25x^2)$ on equispaced nodes. As the polynomial degree increases, oscillations near the boundaries $x = plus.minus 1$ grow unboundedly. The exact function (solid) and interpolants (dashed) are shown for $N = 6$, $10$, and $14$.

figures.label: fig-equipotential-curves
figures.caption: Equipotential curves in the complex plane. Left: uniform node density (equispaced nodes). Right: Chebyshev density, where equipotentials are Bernstein ellipses. The poles of the Runge function at $z = plus.minus 0.2 i$ are marked with crosses. For Chebyshev interpolation, the critical ellipse passing through the poles determines the convergence rate.

figures.label: fig-chebyshev-circle
figures.caption: Geometric construction of Chebyshev points. Points equally spaced on the upper semicircle (by angle $theta_j = j pi / N$) project vertically onto the Chebyshev nodes on the $x$-axis. Equal spacing on the circle maps to clustering near the endpoints $x = plus.minus 1$.

figures.label: fig-chebyshev-success
figures.caption: Chebyshev interpolation of the Runge function. Left: the function and interpolants for $N = 6$, $10$, and $14$. Right: interpolation error on a logarithmic scale. Unlike equispaced interpolation, the error decreases rapidly with increasing $N$.

figures.label: fig-lagrange-basis
figures.caption: Lagrange basis polynomials $L_k (x)$ for $N = 10$. Left: equispaced nodes show large oscillations near the boundaries. Right: Chebyshev nodes yield bounded basis functions throughout the interval.

figures.label: fig-lebesgue-functions
figures.caption: Left: Lebesgue functions $Lambda_(N)(x)$ for $N = 10$ with equispaced, Legendre--Gauss--Lobatto, and Chebyshev nodes. The equispaced case has large peaks near the boundaries. Right: Growth of Lebesgue constants with $N$. The equispaced constant grows exponentially, while the Legendre and Chebyshev constants grow only logarithmically; the dashed curve is the asymptotic formula $frac(2, pi) (ln N + gamma + ln frac(8, pi))$ for the Chebyshev nodes.

figures.label: fig-lebesgue-zoom
figures.caption: Lebesgue constants for Legendre--Gauss--Lobatto and Chebyshev--Gauss--Lobatto nodes (equispaced omitted for clarity). Both grow at the slowest possible rate, $O(ln N)$, and the Legendre--Gauss--Lobatto constant stays below the Chebyshev one. The dashed curves are the asymptotic formula $frac(2, pi) (ln N + gamma + ln frac(8, pi))$ for the Chebyshev nodes and the estimate $frac(2, pi) ln(N + 1) + 0.685$ for the Legendre nodes; the dotted curve is the lower bound $frac(2, pi) ln(N + 1) + 0.5212$ that holds for every node set @Brutman1978. Neither family is optimal, but both stay less than half a unit above this bound.

figures.label: fig-convergence
figures.caption: Convergence comparison for the Runge function. The maximum interpolation error is plotted against polynomial degree $N$ on a semilogarithmic scale. Chebyshev interpolation (green) converges at rate $O(rho^(-N))$ with $rho approx 1.22$. Equispaced interpolation (red) diverges exponentially.

figures.label: fig-convergence-zoom
figures.caption: Chebyshev interpolation convergence for the Runge function (equispaced omitted for clarity). The error decreases geometrically at rate $O(rho^(-N))$ with $rho approx 1.22$, matching the theoretical prediction based on the pole locations at $z = plus.minus 0.2 i$.

figures.label: fig-lebesgue-random
figures.caption: Lebesgue constant for random nodes. Left: growth with polynomial degree $N$ of the median over $200$ draws (gold circles), with the interquartile range (dark shading), the range from the best to the worst draw (light shading) and the exponential law fitted to the median; the equispaced and Chebyshev constants are shown for comparison. Right: distribution of $log_(10)(Lambda_(15))$ over $500$ random trials on a logarithmic scale, revealing the enormous spread spanning many orders of magnitude. Vertical lines mark the median, mean, equispaced, and Chebyshev values.

figures.label: fig-lebesgue-random-chebyshev
figures.caption: Lebesgue constant for "random Chebyshev" nodes (uniform angles projected via cosine). Left: growth with polynomial degree $N$ of the median over $200$ draws (purple circles), with the interquartile range (dark shading), the range from the best to the worst draw (light shading) and the exponential law fitted to the median; the median for uniform random nodes and the equispaced and Chebyshev constants are shown for comparison. Right: distribution of $log_(10)(Lambda_(15))$ over $500$ trials, with its median and mean and the equispaced and Chebyshev values. Despite having the "correct" arcsine marginal distribution, these nodes have typical Lebesgue constants one to three orders of magnitude above those of equispaced nodes.
